facts.fact_text: On 18 April 2000 the applicant organisation informed the Plovdiv Municipality of its intention to hold a public rally on 19 April 2000 in front of the municipality.
The aim of the public rally planned for 19 April 2000 was to protest against the Plovdiv Municipality's actions of uprooting and eradicating the river "Maritza"'s plant life.

The aim of the public rally planned for 19 April 2000 included a demand that the disorderly uprooting and eradication of the river "Maritza"'s plant life be stopped because it was destroying important alluvial trees and the habitat of rare, endangered birds.
The applicant organisation did not hold a rally on 19 April 2000.
In a letter dated 19 April 2000 the Plovdiv Municipality informed the applicant organisation that it would not permit the planned public rally to go ahead.
The letter of 19 April 2000 from the Plovdiv Municipality prohibiting the public rally was signed by the secretary of the municipality.
The full text of the Plovdiv Municipality's letter of 19 April 2000 read: "We inform you that the Plovdiv Municipality does not permit the conducting of the [planned] public rally."
Later on 19 April 2000, police officers visited the offices of the applicant organisation.

On 19 April 2000, police officers obtained signed declarations from the leaders of the applicant organisation stating that they were aware of the prohibition on the planned public rally and would not organise the rally as planned.
The applicant organisation did not hold a rally on 19 April 2000.

In its judgment of 28 March 2001 the Plovdiv Regional Court established that the prohibition of the public rally had been issued in violation of the provisions of the Meetings and Marches Act (1990), as it had been decided not by the mayor but by the secretary of the Plovdiv Municipality.

In its judgment of 28 March 2001 the Plovdiv Regional Court established that the prohibition of the public rally lacked reference to any of the statutory grounds for issuing such prohibitions under the Meetings and Marches Act (1990).

The relevant provisions of the Constitution of Bulgaria (1991) and the Meetings and Marches Act (1990) have been summarised in the Court's judgment in the case of The United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden and Ivanov v. Bulgaria (application no. 44079/98, §§ 72-79, 20 October 2005).

After 19 April 2000, the clearing of the banks and the riverbed of the river "Maritza" by the Plovdiv Municipality continued unabated.
On 26 April 2000 the applicant organisation appealed against the Plovdiv Municipality's prohibition of its public rally.
The applicant organisation's appeal of 26 April 2000 was filed with the Plovdiv Municipality.

The Plovdiv Municipality did not forward the applicant organisation's appeal of 26 April 2000 to the domestic courts together with all relevant documents, as required under the applicable legislation.
On 7 June 2000 the applicant organisation re-filed its appeal against the Plovdiv Municipality's prohibition of the public rally directly with the Plovdiv Regional Court.

On 21 June 2000 the Plovdiv Regional Court requested the Plovdiv Municipality to provide it with its file and all other relevant documents regarding the public rally planned by the applicant organisation.
On 22 June 2000 the Plovdiv Municipality sent the documents requested by the Plovdiv Regional Court, with the exception of the applicant organisation's appeal of 26 April 2000.
On 5 July 2000 the Plovdiv Regional Court requested that the Plovdiv Municipality provide it with the applicant organisation's appeal of 26 April 2000.
On 5 July 2000 the Plovdiv Regional Court instructed the applicant organisation to deposit the required court fee.
The applicant organisation deposited the required court fee on 9 October 2000.
On 25 October 2000 the Plovdiv Municipality provided the Plovdiv Regional Court with the applicant organisation's appeal of 26 April 2000.
At a hearing on 24 January 2001 the Plovdiv Regional Court examined the applicant organisation's appeal against the Plovdiv Municipality's prohibition of the public rally.
In a judgment of 28 March 2001 the Plovdiv Regional Court declared null and void the Plovdiv Municipality's prohibition of the public rally planned by the applicant organisation for 19 April 2000.
The applicant organisation claimed that it was informed of the judgment of the Plovdiv Regional Court of 28 March 2001 on 10 July 2001.
The Government did not challenge the applicant organisation's claim that it was informed of the judgment of the Plovdiv Regional Court of 28 March 2001 on 10 July 2001.
No appeal was filed against the Plovdiv Regional Court's judgment of 28 March 2001.
The Plovdiv Regional Court's judgment of 28 March 2001 became final on an unspecified date.

Before 1 January 2006, the State Responsibility for Damage Act of 1988 provided that the State was liable for damage caused only to private persons by the illegal acts, actions or omissions of its bodies and officials acting within the scope of, or in connection with, their administrative duties (section 1 of the State Responsibility for Damage Act of 1988).

Before 1 January 2006, the State Responsibility for Damage Act of 1988 provided that the State was liable for damage caused only to private persons by the organs of the investigation, the prosecution and the courts (section 2 of the State Responsibility for Damage Act of 1988).

Currently, the State and local municipalities are also liable under section 1 of the State Responsibility for Damage Act of 1988 (as amended) for damage caused to juridical entities by the illegal acts, actions or omissions of their bodies and officials acting within the scope of, or in connection with, their administrative duties.

The amendment to the State Responsibility for Damage Act of 1988 extending liability to damage caused to juridical entities does not have retroactive effect in respect of damage caused prior to its date of introduction.
